name: Vic Smith
bio: Vic Smith was described by the Cow Boy in June 1884 as one of the best hunters, trappers and scouts of the West, who said settlers were getting too thick and talked of going to Alaska. He was still in the area that September, finding a better line for the stage road in September 1884 and giving a petrified mastodon knee joint to the Cow Boy office museum. That October Bob Roberts hired him to collect petrifactions and game for Dakota's exhibit at the New Orleans exposition, and he hunted with the Marquis de Mores, who gave him a rifle; in late 1884 he guided Count Rembielinski on a hunt that took sixty-five deer and antelope. He traveled east in early 1885 but gave up his trip to the New Orleans exposition, then went beaver hunting down the Missouri from the Poplar river, and in May 1885 he and his brother Frank said they would make Medora their home. In July 1885 he went with the Marquise de Mores' hunting party to the Big Horn country, where he was struck with mountain fever, and by January 1886 he and his brother Bill were performing fancy rifle shooting at a Milwaukee dime museum as "Yellowstone Vic" and "Montana Bill."
